findings.title: Out-of-Order / Delayed Webhook Event Triggers Fulfillment Dispatch on Previously Released or Failed Order Sessions
findings.phase: Phase 16: Chaos & Failure Safety & Phase 17: Property & Invariant Testing (Workstream N)
findings.observation: When an order receives a payment.failed webhook event, RazorpayWebhookProcessor.processEvent executes reservationEngine.releaseReservation, which restores mandate budget, restores SKU inventory, and sets the reservation status to 'RELEASED'. If an out-of-order, delayed, or replayed payment.captured webhook event arrives afterwards with a distinct event_id, the processor updates order_sessions.status directly to 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED' via SQL query UPDATE order_sessions SET status = 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED' WHERE intent_id = ?. It then immediately invokes triggerFulfillment(intentId, reservationId, paymentId). The processor does not check whether the current session status is a terminal failed state, nor does it check whether the inventory reservation was already released.
findings.attack_reproduction:
1. Complete a checkout for SKU-MOUSE-PRO (reservation HELD).
2. Dispatch a payment.failed webhook with event_id 'evt_fail_01'. Database updates session to PAYMENT_FAILED and sets reservation to RELEASED.
3. Dispatch a delayed payment.captured webhook with event_id 'evt_late_cap_02'.
4. Database accepts the webhook (HTTP 200 PROCESSED), sets session status to 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED', and triggers fulfillment dispatch, while the underlying reservation remains in 'RELEASED' status with stock restored.
findings.expected: The webhook processing pipeline must enforce monotonic state transitions via FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition and reject any transition from terminal states (PAYMENT_FAILED, REFUNDED, CANCELLED). If commitReservation fails or returns false (reservation is not HELD), the processor must halt fulfillment dispatch and flag the order for manual review.
findings.actual: Runtime accepts payment.captured after payment.failed, transitions session to PAYMENT_CAPTURED, and dispatches fulfillment without holding an active inventory reservation.
findings.impact: HIGH. Risk of phantom order fulfillment, inventory overselling, physical fulfillment of unbacked orders, and financial/physical ledger divergence.
findings.evidence: Empirical chaos test CHAOS-07 in .agents/worker_resilience_quality_2/phase16_chaos_harness.ts confirmed: Reservation status remained 'RELEASED' while order_sessions transitioned to 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED'.
findings.recommendation: In src/rails/webhook.ts lines 105-130: 1. Validate state transition using FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition(orderSession.status, 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED'). Reject invalid transitions with HTTP 409 or return { status: 'ERROR', message: 'Illegal transition from terminal state' }. 2. Require reservationEngine.commitReservation to succeed before calling triggerFulfillment.
findings.regression_test_required: test_delayed_captured_webhook_rejected_on_failed_session: Verify that delivering payment.captured after payment.failed returns an error and prevents fulfillment dispatch.

findings.title: Disconnected Governance Plane False-Pass Risk: V2 Control Plane Unit Tests Test Isolated PDP While Ingress Checkout Bypasses PDP
findings.phase: Phase 19: Test Quality / False-Pass Audit (Workstream P)
findings.observation: In src/core/__tests__/v2_control_plane.test.ts, test '1.2 Blocks checkout when Agent Principal is SUSPENDED or REVOKED' directly calls pdp.evaluateIntent() in isolation, which evaluates the agent principal status and returns DENY (AGENT_SUSPENDED). This test passes (10/10 passing in suite). However, inspection of the actual live HTTP checkout ingress route in src/gateway/router.ts lines 783-803 reveals that POST /v1/agent/checkout calls legacy policyEngine.evaluate() rather than pdp.evaluateIntent(). As a consequence, revoked and suspended agents can successfully execute live checkout transactions over HTTP, even though the unit test suite reports green.
findings.attack_reproduction:
1. Run vitest on v2_control_plane.test.ts: Test '1.2 Blocks checkout when Agent Principal is SUSPENDED or REVOKED' passes.
2. In runtime, register an agent with status 'REVOKED'.
3. Send an HTTP POST to /v1/agent/checkout with a signed mandate.
4. Router executes policyEngine.evaluate(), which passes.
5. Router acquires reservation and creates Razorpay order, returning HTTP 201 Created.
findings.expected: Unit and integration tests must exercise the live HTTP ingress endpoints (POST /v1/agent/checkout and POST /v1/agent/ingress/:protocol) to verify that agent status, trust level, and capability limits are strictly enforced during live checkout.
findings.actual: Unit test evaluates PDP in isolation and passes, creating a dangerous false-pass impression that revoked agents are blocked from commercial execution.
findings.impact: HIGH. False sense of security in automated test suite; rogue or compromised agents continue to authorize transactions despite automated tests passing.
findings.evidence: v2_control_plane.test.ts line 119 invokes pdp.evaluateIntent(intent, defaultPolicy, 'agent_rogue_01') directly, while router.ts line 784 invokes policyEngine.evaluate(intent.mandate, truthResult.totalAmount, truthResult.categories, activePolicy.merchant_id).
findings.recommendation: Wire POST /v1/agent/checkout to pdp.evaluateIntent() before acquiring reservations. Refactor test 1.2 to inject an HTTP POST request to /v1/agent/checkout and assert HTTP 403 rejection.
findings.regression_test_required: test_http_checkout_rejects_suspended_or_revoked_agent: Send HTTP POST to /v1/agent/checkout with an agent principal marked SUSPENDED and assert HTTP 403 rejection.

findings.title: Malformed Payment Rail Response Handling Accepts Null Order ID and Corrupts Session Reconciliation
findings.observation: In src/gateway/router.ts line 856, the gateway invokes railClient.createOrder(). If the payment rail returns a malformed response where id is null or undefined, the router does not validate that razorpayOrder.id is a non-empty string. It executes INSERT INTO order_sessions (...) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ...) with razorpay_order_id = null. In src/store/db.ts line 82, razorpay_order_id has a UNIQUE constraint but lacks NOT NULL. The gateway returns HTTP 201 Created with razorpay_order_id: null.
findings.attack_reproduction:
1. Mock or intercept railClient.createOrder to return { id: null, entity: 'order', amount: 350000, status: 'created' }.
2. Submit a valid checkout request to POST /v1/agent/checkout.
3. Gateway commits order session to database with razorpay_order_id = null and returns HTTP 201 Created.
4. When webhook arrives from payment rail referencing the real order ID, it cannot be matched to the session.
findings.expected: Fail-closed. The gateway must validate that the provider order response contains a non-empty string identifier. If missing, it must abort order session insertion, roll back dual reservations, log RAIL_RESPONSE_MALFORMED in audit ledger, and return HTTP 502 PAYMENT_RAIL_ERROR.
findings.actual: Gateway accepts malformed response with null order ID, retains dual-resource reservations, and returns HTTP 201 Created.
findings.impact: MEDIUM. Ghost orders, unreconcilable database state, and failure of subsequent webhook matching.
findings.evidence: Empirical chaos test CHAOS-08 in phase16_chaos_harness.ts confirmed: Status 201 returned with razorpay_order_id recorded as null.
findings.recommendation:
1. In src/gateway/router.ts line 867, add: if (!razorpayOrder?.id || typeof razorpayOrder.id !== 'string') { throw new Error('Payment rail returned malformed response: missing order ID'); }.
2. In src/store/db.ts line 82, alter schema: razorpay_order_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL.
findings.regression_test_required: test_malformed_order_response_rolls_back_and_fails_closed: Mock railClient to return null ID, assert HTTP 502 response, and assert reservation is RELEASED.

findings.title: Continuous Integration Workflow Omits Explicit Least-Privilege Permissions Block
findings.observation: In .github/workflows/ci.yml, the workflow defines the 'verify' job running build, test, pentest, audit:verify, and benchmark steps. However, it completely omits a top-level or job-level 'permissions:' directive. By default in GitHub Actions, workflows without explicit permissions inherit repository-default write permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN, creating supply chain escalation risks if dependencies or build scripts are compromised.
findings.attack_reproduction: Inspect .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 9-14: Job 'verify' specifies 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' and proceeds directly to 'steps:' without declaring permissions.
findings.expected: Workflows must adhere to OpenSSF / SLSA least privilege standards by declaring top-level: permissions: contents: read.
findings.actual: Permissions directive is omitted, relying on implicit GitHub repository defaults.
findings.impact: LOW. Security posture weakness and violation of GitHub Actions supply chain best practices.
findings.recommendation:
Add explicit top-level permissions block to .github/workflows/ci.yml:
permissions:
  contents: read
findings.regression_test_required: Workflow schema validation checking for explicit permissions block in all .github/workflows/*.yml files.

findings.title: Performance Benchmark Baseline 303.81 ms Evaluates Single-Iteration Cold Boot with In-Memory Mock Rather than Live End-to-End Latency
findings.observation: The canonical repository benchmark metric (303.81 ms baseline; empirically reproduced at 301.98 ms and 282.96 ms) measures a single cold-start iteration using Fastify in-memory injection (app.inject), an in-memory SQLite database (:memory:), and an offline deterministic mock Razorpay order generator (isLiveCredentials == false). Framework boot and plugin initialization account for ~237 - 250 ms (~83%) of the duration, while the actual checkout transaction takes 41 - 47 ms cold and 3 - 10 ms warm. Crucially, it does not include OS TCP/TLS network stack overhead or external HTTP roundtrips to Razorpay sandbox endpoints (which typically add 200 - 500 ms).
findings.attack_reproduction: Run npm run benchmark. Milestones printed: 1. Gateway Boot & Policy Engine: 250.56 ms; 2. Catalog Ingestion: 0.55 ms; 3. Ed25519 Mandate Sign: 3.44 ms; 4. 6-Phase Agent Checkout: 47.42 ms; Total: 301.98 ms.
findings.expected: Performance documentation should explicitly distinguish framework cold-start boot latency from warm transaction processing latency, and state that external bank rail network latency is excluded.
findings.actual: Documentation presents 303.81 ms as a single monolithic metric without qualifying that 83% of the time is Node.js/Fastify cold-start initialization.
findings.impact: INFORMATIONAL. Potential misinterpretation of architectural throughput and latency characteristics.
findings.evidence: Source review of src/demo/benchmark.ts lines 17, 28, 64 and empirical benchmark stdout.
findings.recommendation: Publish separate metrics: (1) Cold-Start Initialization: ~250 ms, (2) Core Authorization Engine Latency (p50: ~4 ms, p95: ~8 ms, p99: ~15 ms), and (3) Projected Live Network Transaction Latency (~300 - 550 ms).

findings.title: External Tool Disclosure: Assessment Utilized Strix-Informed Methodology Without Independent Strix Binary Execution
findings.phase: Phase 21: External Tool / Strix Disclosure (Workstream P)
findings.observation: The penetration test reports and security control matrices cite Strix priorities across 14 security invariants. In-depth inspection confirms that no Strix binary, CLI agent, or automated scanning tool was executed against the repository. The pentest suite was implemented and executed entirely through custom TypeScript code in src/demo/pentest_runner.ts.
findings.attack_reproduction: Search repository for Strix executable, CLI invocation, or scan artifact outputs. None exist.
findings.expected: External tool citations must strictly adhere to Phase 21 labeling: STRIX-INFORMED METHODOLOGY vs INDEPENDENT STRIX SCAN.
findings.actual: Footnotes in PENTEST_REPORT.md correctly mention methodology-informed assessment, but summary tables and headers must maintain consistent labeling to avoid auditor ambiguity.
findings.evidence: PENTEST_REPORT.md:60: '(methodology-driven assessment; external binary agent not independently executed)'.
findings.recommendation: Enforce standardized label across all audit documentation: 'STRIX-INFORMED METHODOLOGY (Independent external scanner binary was not executed)'.
